notes: How detection works in the game today (src/simulation/press/matters.ts): a monthly committee report lists payments to the candidate 30 days after they are made; a rival weighs rivalry (moderate), the payments on the report (strong if more than one) and 'could be a reimbursement' (slight or moderate) and may complain; the state body's own review flags reported payments 45 to 120 days after filing (placeholder per state); a paid bookkeeper, if any, first raises it privately, then may report outside if the payments continue.

How a case proceeds (src/simulation/press/procedures.ts GENERATED_STATE_OVERSIGHT): complaint received or review opened, respondent notified, answer period closed, preliminary inquiry, then findings or dismissal. Step lengths are placeholders drawn per state: 7-21, 14-30, 21-60 and 30-120 days.

Disposition today is deterministic: supported only when an actual payment with record evidence exists (procedures.ts institutionHoldsSupport), and then always a finding. ChatGPT's C04 rejected fixed conviction odds, so a replacement should be a rule, not a probability, if the research allows.

Consequences today (src/simulation/press/finding-consequences.ts, findings.ts): 300 basis points of contest share lost in an open race, handed evenly to rivals, never below 1 point; +50% per earlier finding up to 3x; 90 off a later race's starting weight (850-1150 scale) for six years; restitution of every payment found; a civil penalty per payment drawn per state from $500 to $5,000, doubled for a second finding, only where the body's profile is generated.
question: For campaign-finance cases alleging personal use of campaign money that reach a state regulator or the FEC, what share end in dismissal, admonishment or warning, settlement or conciliation, or a formal finding with penalty, and what drives the difference (amount, repeat conduct, cooperation, the respondent's answer)? Separately: the earlier answer (ethics-finding-electoral-magnitudes) found no universal vote penalty for a finding, only the 6 to 11 point Peters and Welch range for corruption charges. Given the game models a finding as a single support shift in the race under way, what defensible rule should it use (a range by conduct type and timing, a dependence on coverage, or none), and should it scale with the amount taken?
requestedBy: Consequences for corruption and laws thread

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: No universal vote penalty for an official finding; the 6-11 point range is for charges in 1968-1978 House races. Says nothing about how often cases end without a finding.

title: How campaign-money cases actually end, and what a finding should cost in the game
usableAnswer: (1) Disposition shares or at least an ordering (dismissal, warning, conciliation, finding) with the factors that move a case between them, per body where known. (2) A rule for the in-race support cost of a public finding the game can apply, with the factors it depends on, or an explicit statement that no rule is supported and why.
whyItMatters: The owner asked on 2026-09-22 whether a finding always brings punishment and how the lost points are calculated. Today every case with a real recorded payment ends in a finding, which is too certain, and a finding costs a flat 3 points (4.5 for a repeat) regardless of the amount, the coverage or the timing.
